taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO; Texas is within the native state-level range, but the project currently has only one defensible target-zone county after excluding Williamson from the target list.
look_here_first: Check the petiole glands and leaf margin before the huge flower. Maypop has two conspicuous nectar glands on the petiole, broad deeply 3-lobed leaves with serrated margins, and a very large purple-and-white corona flower.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis is herbarium-backed. Williamson was present in the older review but is outside the project target zone and is not counted. No second or third target-zone wild county is currently locked.

approval_exception.reason: Learner admission is independent from native-range certification. Preserve the scientific HOLD.

best_field_traits: vigorous perennial climbing or trailing vine with axillary tendrils
two conspicuous sessile extrafloral nectary glands on the petiole
lobes broad, pointed, and distinctly serrate
large solitary flower with purple-and-white multi-whorled corona
large ovoid to subglobose maypop fruit
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Separate from P. lutea by petiole glands, serrated broad lobes, and huge flowers; separate from P. tenuiloba by the broad serrated lobes and large showy flower.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Paired petiole glands + broad serrated lobes + very large corona flower and fruit are the strongest combination.
